en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Ujjagghikavagga 16.
The Second Training Rule on Swinging the Body.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas swaying their bodies, letting their bodies hang down...
[and so forth]. "The training is to be observed: 'I shall not sit in an inhabited area swaying my body.
One must not sit in an inhabited area swaying one's body."
One should sit with the body held erect.
Whoever, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area shaking the body or letting the body hang down, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense—
Unintentionally,
through lack of mindfulness,
or not knowing.
For one who is ill,
for one who has entered upon the rains residence,
and in times of distress.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
